title: I can’t believe we are only a few days away from first preview!!!! #I...
transcript: Immersive Phantom begins previews on Thursday. And while there's still a little bit of mystery around what the experience is actually going to entail, here's everything we know so far about how it's gonna be laid out. This is part of a public filing that they made with the city for some of the construction that they wanna do associated with this project. And this includes some renderings as well as a full floor plan. You can see that this is going to be a four floor experience, including a cellar and a roof. So this thing is going to be massive. And while it's really hard to tell what each space is going to be used for, we can make some educated guesses. So, for example, I don't think it's a huge leap to say the cellar is probably going to be the Phantom's underground lair. The first floor, which seems to be the lobby of the theater. The second floor, which I'm going to assume is where the actual auditorium is, although it's kind of hard to tell, but this is the only floor with a mezzanine. And so I'm assuming the tall ceilings are to accommodate the falling chandelier. And then we have the third floor, which I'm going to assume is like dressing rooms and a backstage area. The fourth floor, which also accesses the lower roof. And then finally the upper roof. The other thing of note is we actually have a mockup of what The roof. Roof top is going to look like. This is, I believe, going to be the lower roof area, and then there is another upper roof area. And given the cemetery vibes, I'm assuming this is are they're going to sing wishing you were somehow here again. We've actually been able to see a little bit of what this looks like from the street, and it does look like the roof area will be at least partially covered. Also makes me wonder if you'll be able to hear the rooftop performances from the street. So who knows? Maybe this will be the next Avita balcony, and people will stand on the street to listen to them sing wishing you are somehow here again every night. We also know that this is going to be more of a guided experience rather than the free roam of something like sleep no more. The production describes it as a journey from room to room, up and down several flights of stairs, with some rooms where you will be seated and others where you will be standing or allowed to move about, although there will be ADA options available for anyone who cannot take the stairs or needs a more consistent seat.
